reviewer: Claude Code (Opus 5.5) with a fresh-context medium reviewer subagent

claims.summary: Pair occupancy: in the charged character window (any graph, multigraphs included), for s vectors psi_i of support exactly two on pairwise disjoint edge pairs, W their span, pi the largest number of paired edges at a vertex, beta_W = 2 sqrt(K/(m - s)) and eta_W = (1 + 2 beta_W^(epsilon - pi))^n - 1, if 2K + 2s <= 2D and 4K < m - s then the number q_W(K) of cosets of the cut space plus W met by the support-K ball satisfies (1 - eta_W) B_(m-s)(K) <= q_W(K) <= B_(m-s)(K): each pair is one merged coordinate of the quotient by W, whose nonzero classes have representatives of support one, and the cut of a small potential keeps at least (epsilon - pi) times its support of unpaired edges, so good classes lie in distinct cosets.
claims.assessment: Working proof by the good-character union bound of lem:high-incidence-occupancy run on the classes of the quotient by W, the paired edges discarded.
claims.rationale: The per-pair occupancy at which the approximator product goal review's decisive test stopped; it refines the edge-set counts, B_(m-2s), to B_(m-s) for pair spans beyond lem:local-tuple-ratio's window.
claims.next_action: The rank profile of the products inside one sector, starting with sectors whose good representative touches no pair.

claims.summary: Pair sector bounds: in lem:pair-occupancy's setting with pi < epsilon, for a nonzero P in the span of the characters of W of support at most e, K + e <= D, with c(k) the rank of f -> R_D(P f) on degree <= k and c_C(k) that rank on the characters of support <= k of a coset C of B + W: (i) c(k) = sum_C c_C(k) (lem:cut-code-sectors with S = (W+B)/B); (ii) 1 <= c_C(k) <= min(n_C(k), 3^s), W meeting B only in 0, so q_W(k) <= c(k) <= min(h(k), 3^s q_W(k)) for k <= K; (iii) the two ratio bounds these give, 3^s q_W(K-d)/q_W(K) and h(K-d)/q_W(K), exceed h(K-d)/h(K) by at least 3^s (1 - eta_W)(1 - eta_occ) and (1 - eta_occ)(1 - q) e^(sK/m), q = K/(2(m-s-K+1)), using that ball ratios B_n'(k-d)/B_n'(k) do not fall when coordinates are removed. (i) and (ii) need only K + e <= D, s <= D and pi < epsilon; (iii) also needs the lemma's hypotheses at levels K-d and K and eta_occ < 1. On the power-growing charged family, for D/2 < s <= D - K and pi <= Delta/8, both factors are N^(Omega(n)), so these two bounds built from c_C >= 1 cannot give the decisive test's yes outcome; a block form combining the counts with the ranks of P inside the sectors is not covered.
claims.assessment: Working composition of lem:cut-code-sectors, lem:cut-code-classes, the new lemma and lem:cut-ball-occupancy, with an elementary ball-ratio monotonicity.
claims.rationale: Shows that the two ratio bounds built from c_C >= 1 and the coset counts, now sharp up to 1 - eta_W, cannot give the yes outcome of the decisive test in the stated range, so a yes needs bounds on the ranks of the products inside the sectors.
claims.next_action: The rank profile of P inside the sectors whose good representative touches no pair, a question in the group algebra of F_3^s.
